cells.quote: The instrument type and the assessed domains are clearly related, according to a cross‐cutting examination of these data. In particular, the scope of ad hoc questionnaires (n = 25) was virtually limited to practical CPR techniques (ventilations and compressions). O.outcome_detail: retention of BLS knowledge over subsequent months

result.effect: 16/36 studies assessed retention; most reported rapid deterioration within months

cells.quote: Pre‐ and immediately post intervention assessment was the most common evaluation method. Only 16 of the 36 studies assessed knowledge retention over time, with follow‐up periods generally ranging from 1 to 6 months. This presents a significant challenge from an educational planning perspective: school health programs should incorporate mandatory annual or semiannual refresher sessions into the curriculum rather than relying on one‐off interventions, given that most studies confirm that knowledge of basic life support (BLS) deteriorates rapidly within a matter of months.
cells.note: Narrative synthesis of follow-up studies; no pooled effect size was reported.
